rows.title: An AAL1 session issued before its factor became unusable stays valid until normal expiry or revocation (probe P-H)
rows.disposition: Approved residual design limit. Such a session is bounded by the idle and 12 hour absolute lifetimes and by explicit revocation, and it carries no sensitive authority: sensitive writes require the account's required-assurance floor and step-up, and the factor that became unusable cannot satisfy it. Revoking sessions on every factor-state change would alter the approved session lifecycle, so no code change is made; the parity of the two verifiers (TestSkipMFASessionParityAfterFactorBecomesUnusable) is the regression that keeps the floor identical on the issuance and verification sides.
rows.rationale: Changing it would change the approved session lifecycle (architecture). The residual grants nothing beyond what the same session had before the factor became unusable.

The permanent in-repo tests drive real issued sessions through the shared Authorizer and the operations service.
acceptance: TestOpsFollowStreamEndsOnEveryRealSessionRevocationPath (C2R-O1) and TestIssuedSessionsAreAcceptedAndRejectedIdenticallyByTheAuthorizerVerifier; C2 run442 report H09-H09e (reviewer probe, recorded evidence).

rows.title: Existing ambiguous revoked second factors keep the assurance floor at 2; such accounts need the approved restricted recovery

AUTH-08-L4 adds the pre-confirmation warning for the related last-working-factor case; the floor is not lowered.
rows.rationale: Lowering the floor for ambiguous history would weaken the approved assurance rule.

rows.rationale: Additive-column posture shared by every migration; a down path that preserved provenance would need a new schema element.

rows.rationale: Fail-closed is the approved safety property; a silent persistent recovery of an unrecorded report would have to guess state.
